nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Tokyo Institute of Technology (Institute of Science Tokyo), Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics / strongly correlated electron systems and superconductivity
motivation: In 2006-2008 Hideo Hosono discovered superconductivity in the layered iron oxypnictides LaFeAsO and LaFeAsO1-xFx (Tc = 26 K). This overturned the long-held view that magnetic iron is hostile to superconductivity. Within months, Tc in the family rose above 55 K. It was the first new class of high-temperature superconductors since the cuprates, and it opened a whole field worldwide. Iron pnictides and chalcogenides became a second platform for studying unconventional pairing mediated by spin fluctuations, multiorbital correlation, nematicity and, later, topological superconductivity in Fe(Te,Se). The discovery shows materials-driven physics at its best: chemical design of a new crystal reveals an unexpected collective quantum state, with results reproduced in hundreds of laboratories. It also advances superconducting wires and tapes for energy-efficient technology. Hosono's broader record of functional materials design, including the transparent amorphous oxide semiconductors now used in displays, underlines the depth of this contribution.
